observations.why: First-person plural present continuous performs a settled course of action the speaker expects others to follow — ratification language, not a position being argued for.
Flat unhedged assertions presented as justification for the switch, but no performed settling — these are claims ready to defend, moveable with evidence.
Performed declarative recording the migration as a settled item in a decision summary — the act of ratifying, not arguing for.
Restated performance claim in summary form — asserted as fact but not performed as a settled decision; the gain is a claim supporting the decision, not the decision itself.
Performed declarative fixing a schedule for the migration — ratifying a timeline is a settling act, not an argued position.
